questions.q: What term describes a chemical reaction that releases thermal energy to the surroundings, causing the temperature to rise?
Which of the following processes is always endothermic?
What happens to the surroundings during an endothermic reaction?
a: They gain thermal energy and heat up
They remain at a constant temperature
They lose thermal energy, causing the temperature to drop

questions.q: In an energy level diagram (reaction pathway diagram) for an exothermic reaction, how does the energy of the products compare to the energy of the reactants?
a: Products have higher energy than reactants
Products have equal energy to reactants
Energy first drops and then rises infinitely
Products have lower energy than reactants

questions.q: What is activation energy?
a: The minimum amount of energy particles must collide with to start a chemical reaction
The total energy released during bond formation
The heat absorbed when a liquid turns into a gas
The electrical energy required to run electrolysis

questions.q: Why is energy absorbed during the bond-breaking phase of a chemical reaction?
a: Energy is created by splitting atoms
Energy must be supplied to overcome the electrostatic forces holding the bonded atoms together
Energy is absorbed to cool the reaction down
Electrons are destroyed in the process

questions.q: How is overall enthalpy change (Delta H) calculated in terms of bond energies?
a: Energy released in breaking bonds minus energy absorbed in forming bonds
Total energy of products multiplied by total energy of reactants
Energy absorbed in breaking bonds minus energy released in forming bonds
Sum of all bond energies in the entire system

questions.q: What sign is given to the enthalpy change (Delta H) for an exothermic reaction?
Which of the following reactions is classified as exothermic?
a: Neutralization between hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide

questions.q: What does a catalyst do to the activation energy of a chemical reaction?
a: Lowers the activation energy by providing an alternative reaction pathway
Keeps the activation energy completely unchanged
Eliminates activation energy entirely so no collisions are needed

questions.q: Which of the following processes represents an endothermic energy change?
In an endothermic reaction energy profile diagram, what is represented by the vertical height from the reactants line to the peak of the curve?
a: Activation energy for the forward reaction

questions.q: What occurs during bond formation in a chemical reaction?
a: Energy is released to the surroundings
Energy is absorbed from the surroundings

questions.q: Which of the following statements about bond energies is correct?
a: Bond breaking is an exothermic process
Bond making is an exothermic process
Bond breaking and bond making both release energy
Bond breaking and bond making both absorb energy

questions.q: If a reaction has more energy released during bond formation than was absorbed during bond breaking, what type of reaction is it?
Which device is used in the laboratory to measure the temperature change during solution reactions or neutralization?
Why does a simple chemical cell (battery) generate electrical energy?
a: Exothermic redox reactions convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy
Endothermic reactions absorb electricity from the air
Heat from the room boils electrolyte solutions
Friction between metal plates creates static electricity

questions.q: During the thermal decomposition of copper(II) carbonate, what type of heat change is observed in the test tube?
a: Exothermic because heat is generated rapidly
Endothermic because heat must be continuously supplied from a Bunsen burner

questions.q: Which of the following everyday items utilizes an exothermic chemical reaction?
a: Instant cold pack for sports injuries

questions.q: What is the primary role of a fuel cell, such as a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell?
a: To store electrical charges like a standard capacitor
To burn hydrogen gas explosively to produce mechanical thrust
To decompose water into hydrogen and oxygen using heat
To generate electrical energy directly from the combustion of a fuel without burning it

questions.q: How does increasing the temperature of a reaction mixture affect the energy of the colliding particles?
a: It increases the kinetic energy and speed of particles, leading to more frequent and energetic successful collisions
It decreases particle movement to stabilize bonds
It reduces the activation energy barrier

questions.q: What is the enthalpy change (Delta H) sign for an endothermic process?
Which reaction represents a typical combustion process that is strongly exothermic?
In a reaction profile diagram, what does the difference in height between the reactants line and the products line represent?
Why do chemical reactions require an initial input of activation energy?
a: To overcome repulsive forces between electron clouds and start breaking existing chemical bonds
To cool the reactants down to stable temperatures
To increase the mass of the products

questions.q: Which of the following processes is used in instant cold packs for sports injuries due to its strong endothermic nature?
a: Dissolving ammonium nitrate salt in water

questions.q: What happens to the temperature of water when sodium hydroxide pellets are dissolved in it?
a: Temperature rises because the dissolution is exothermic

questions.q: Which factor determines whether a chemical reaction is exothermic or endothermic overall?
a: The physical state of the reactants only
The presence of a platinum catalyst
The atmospheric pressure in the laboratory
The relative magnitude of energy absorbed in breaking bonds versus energy released in forming new bonds

questions.q: When hydrogen and oxygen react to form water vapor, energy is released. What does this indicate about the bonds in reactants versus products?
a: The bonds formed in water are stronger than the bonds broken in hydrogen and oxygen
The bonds in the reactants are stronger than the bonds in the products
No bonds are formed during this reaction

questions.q: Which of the following statements about catalysts in energy changes is correct?
a: Catalysts change the overall enthalpy change (Delta H) of a reaction
Catalysts lower the activation energy by providing an alternative reaction route
Catalysts make endothermic reactions become exothermic
Catalysts are consumed permanently during bond formation

questions.q: If 50 cm<sup>3</sup> of acid is neutralized by 50 cm<sup>3</sup> of alkali and the temperature increases by 6 degrees Celsius, what type of reaction has occurred?
Which of the following energy changes is expected when bonds with high bond energies are formed from atoms?
a: A small amount of energy is absorbed
A large amount of energy is released

questions.q: What is the primary energy transformation occurring in a car engine during the combustion of petrol?
a: Chemical energy to thermal and kinetic mechanical energy
Thermal energy to gravitational potential energy

questions.q: Why does a glowing splint reignite in oxygen? (Considering energy and collision factors)
a: Oxygen cools the splint down rapidly
Higher concentration of oxygen increases successful collision frequency and rate of exothermic combustion
Oxygen absorbs all heat from the splint

questions.q: In bond energy calculations, if the total energy required to break bonds is 1200 kJ/mol and the total energy released in forming bonds is 1500 kJ/mol, what is the enthalpy change (Delta H)?
Which term describes the energy needed to break one mole of a particular covalent bond in gaseous molecules?
What is observed when solid ammonium chloride is dissolved in water inside a beaker?
a: The beaker feels cold because the process is endothermic
The beaker feels hot because the process is exothermic

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the role of activation energy in a stable mixture of hydrogen and oxygen gases at room temperature?
a: It is zero, so they react instantaneously
It is high enough that without a spark or flame, the molecules do not collide with sufficient energy to react
It causes the gases to liquefy
It absorbs all thermal energy from the container

questions.q: During photosynthesis, plants absorb light energy from the Sun to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose. How is this reaction classified?
What is the main advantage of using a catalyst in industrial exothermic processes, such as the Haber process?
a: It increases the final yield of products infinitely
It eliminates the need for any containers
It allows the reaction to proceed faster at lower temperatures, saving energy and operational costs
